markers.label: Mostar
markers.description: Mostar became the war's most visible urban fracture between former Croat and Bosniak allies.

markers.label: Central Bosnia
markers.description: Mixed towns in the Lašva Valley and central Bosnia became the core battlefield.

slides.title: Origins and Road to War
slides.cap: Visual reference for Origins and Road to War.
slides.body: The Croat-Bosniak War grew from the collapse of cooperation inside Bosnia's wider war. Former allies against Bosnian Serb forces began fighting over territory, command authority, supply routes, and incompatible political futures.

markers.label: Mostar
markers.description: The ambush belongs to the breakdown of cooperation among HVO, ARBiH, and local armed formations around Mostar.

slides.title: Kavanjina Ambush
slides.body: The Kavanjina Ambush belongs to the early rupture around Mostar, where local alliances among HVO, ARBiH, and HOS forces broke down. The event signaled that mistrust could turn quickly into armed confrontation.

markers.label: Ahmići
markers.description: Ahmići became one of the defining atrocity sites of the Croat-Bosniak War.

slides.title: Ahmići massacre
slides.body: The Ahmići massacre became one of the war's defining atrocities. Civilians were targeted in a village that symbolized how mixed communities could be destroyed by military plans and ethnic cleansing.

markers.label: Trusina
markers.description: The Trusina killings show that atrocities were committed against civilians and prisoners on both sides of the conflict.

slides.title: Trusina massacre
slides.body: The Trusina massacre showed that the violence was not one-directional. Bosniak forces killed Croat civilians and prisoners, adding another layer of fear, revenge, and accountability to the conflict.

markers.label: Zenica
markers.description: The shelling of Zenica's market area brought the wider Bosnian war's urban civilian vulnerability into the Croat-Bosniak front.

slides.title: Zenica massacre
slides.body: The Zenica massacre brought civilian vulnerability into sharp focus. Shelling in an urban area showed how people far from front-line trenches could still become targets or victims of battlefield escalation.

markers.label: Vrbanja / Vitez area
markers.description: The Vitez area saw repeated violence against civilians as front lines hardened inside mixed communities.

slides.title: Vrbanja massacre
slides.body: The Vrbanja massacre reflected the lethal fragmentation around Vitez and central Bosnia. Localized killing hardened front lines and made later coexistence much harder.

slides.title: Mokronoge massacre
slides.body: Mokronoge illustrates the war's smaller atrocity geography: places outside the most famous headlines still carried grief, fear, and postwar demands for recognition.

markers.label: Stupni Do

slides.cap: Visual reference for Stupni Do massacre.

slides.body: Križančevo Selo became part of Croat memory of victimhood in central Bosnia. Its place in the timeline matters because the war's atrocities shaped both justice processes and competing public memory.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Croat-Bosniak War

markers.label: Mostar bridge line
markers.description: Mostar's divided cityscape turned a local front into an international symbol of cultural and communal rupture.

markers.label: Washington
markers.description: US diplomacy helped push Croat and Bosniak leaders into the Washington Agreement.

slides.title: International and Human Dimensions
slides.cap: Visual reference for International and Human Dimensions.
slides.body: International pressure, humanitarian reporting, and US diplomacy helped push the sides toward the Washington Agreement. For civilians, the war meant detention, massacres, divided towns, destroyed homes, and broken mixed communities.

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Croat-Bosniak War ended and what followed

markers.label: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
markers.description: The Washington Agreement ended Croat-Bosniak fighting by creating a federation that could fight beside Bosnian government forces.

slides.title: Outcome and Legacy
slides.cap: Visual reference for Outcome and Legacy.
slides.body: The Washington Agreement ended Croat-Bosniak fighting and created the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It turned former enemies back into military partners, but it did not erase the trauma of the war within the war.
